title: The illustrators, ii
logline: Osaka's letter: a drawing of the dog, from the strip, in a line Wood doesn't have. He pins it beside Lyon's glow. Three strangers on the wall now.

panels.composition: The garage. WOOD opening an airmail envelope. BARNABY on the floor. Two drawings already on the wall — Lyon (the ridge glow), Montreal (the dock).

image.prompt: a man at a drafting table opening a thin airmail envelope, an old dog on the floor, two strangers' drawings pinned on the wall beside him, razor-sharp ink

panels.composition: The drawing from Osaka: Barnaby, under a table, in a brush line — looser, wetter, better at the dog than Wood is. Wood's face.

image.prompt: close-up of a man looking at a stranger's loose wet brush drawing of an old dog under a table, his face still
image.notes: The Osaka drawing should look better than the strip's own dog. Different hand.

panels.composition: Wood looking from the drawing to the actual dog. The dog looking back. The drawing is right.

image.prompt: a man holding a drawing up beside an old dog and comparing them, the dog looking back

panels.composition: Three drawings on the wall: Lyon, Montreal, Osaka. Wood pinning the third. Then — a glance over his shoulder at the empty garage. Someone is looking closely.

image.prompt: a man pinning a third drawing beside two others on a garage wall and glancing over his shoulder at the empty room behind him, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: 'I never got your ear.' Three strangers on the wall. The glance over the shoulder.
